sentences.text: Researchers investigated how mutations in the ALMS1 gene, which cause Alström syndrome, affect cellular structures, noting that the ALMS1 protein is located at the proximal end of centrioles.
In cells lacking ALMS1, centrioles became shorter and often fractured at their proximal ends, while also showing decreased microtubule-organizing activity and damaged centriole linkers.
This absence impaired the transport of Golgi-derived cargo to the centrosome, a process critical for assembling the transition zone, forming cilia, and regulating ciliary membrane composition.
In a mouse model, disrupting ALMS1 led to a progressive, age-dependent loss of cilia in the retina, kidney, and brain.
The authors conclude that Alström syndrome results from disrupted proximal centriole integrity and impaired protein trafficking to the centrosome, which compromises ciliary assembly and maintenance.
